newsitem.title: USA: USA Waste to buy United Waste.
newsitem.headline: USA Waste to buy United Waste.

text.p: USA Waste Services Inc and United Waste Systems Inc said Monday they had signed a definitive agreement for USA Waste to buy United Waste in a stock swap valued at $1.7 billion.
United Waste shareholders will receive 1.075 shares of USA Waste common for each United Waste common share, they said.
The deal is expected to close during the third quarter, the companies said.
After the merger, USA Waste will have annual revenues of about $2.1 billion and total assets in excess of $4.5 billion, they said.
United Waste will designate two persons to the board of USA Waste.

The existing senior management team of USA Waste -- John Drury, chairman and chief executive officer; Rodney Proto, president and chief operating officer; and Earl DeFrates, executive vice president and chief financial officer -- will retain their respective positions in the merged company.

United Waste's senior management team -- including Bradley Jacobs, chairman and chief executive officer; John Milne, vice chairman and chief acquisition officer; and Michael Nolan, chief financial officer -- will assist the merged company with transition matters and future acquisitions, the companies said.

Drury said, "We are very pleased to be combining with a company as successful as United Waste. We anticipate significant synergies and enhanced growth opportunities to result from this merger, which we expect will be accretive to our earnings."

The companies said the merger's closing is subject to stockholder approval, qualification of the merger as a tax-free pooling-of-interests transaction, antitrust clearance, and other customary conditions.
Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp acted as USA Waste's financial adviser. Goldman, Sachs & Co acted as financial adviser to United Waste.

Following the merger, the companies will operate 155 landfills, 270 collection companies, and 153 transfer stations, serving over three million customers in 42 states, the District of Columbia, Canada, Mexico, and Puerto Rico.
